### `[mcp.agent]`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime` | `"auto"` | sdk \| cli \| auto -- 'sdk' uses claude_agent_sdk in-process, 'cli' shells out to `claude -p`, 'auto' prefers the SDK and falls back to the CLI. |
| `model` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_MODEL:-}"` |  |
| `unusable_markers` | `[]` | Extra wordings that mean "this runtime cannot serve ANY request" -- the model is not enabled on this deployment, the credential is refused, the quota is gone.  Added to the built-in patterns rather than replacing them, because the phrasing comes from whichever runtime is installed. The class exists because its absence cost a whole run.  `claude-opus-5-5` was not enabled on the operator's Vertex project, so every agent call returned 404 carrying its own fix -- "Try --model to switch to claude-opus-5".  It matched none of the other classes ("not available", not "unavailable"), so it was read as an ordinary failure: retried three times a stage, four stages a target, thirteen targets -- and every one of them silently degraded to the deterministic pipeline.  The remedy appeared 29 times in the log and never once as a conclusion. A failure about the installation is the same for every stage and every target, so the answer is not a different attempt.  It is to stop attempting, say so once, and carry on deterministically. |
| `credential_refresh` | `true` | A failure the model's *credential* causes is also a fact about the installation, and one that can often be fixed without anybody typing: see [mcp.agent.credential_failures.*] below.  When one of those profiles recognises a failure, its refresh command is tried once for the whole run; if that works the stage retries without spending an attempt, and if it does not, agents stop for the rest of the run and the final verdict names the addresses that lost them, the profile's remedy, and the command that re-runs exactly those addresses.  false never runs a refresh (the latch still applies). |
| `credential_refresh_timeout_seconds` | `60` | Wall clock for one refresh command, unless its profile sets timeout_seconds. |
| `error_chars` | `600` | How much of a failed agent run's message to keep.  Enough for the sentence naming the remedy -- which is the only reason the message is kept at all. |
| `capture_stderr` | `true` | What the CLI under the SDK writes to stderr is kept (the last stderr_lines, redacted) and named when the SDK fails: its own error only said "Check stderr output for details", and the reason was never seen. |
| `sdk_cli` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_SDK_CLI:-auto}"` | Which Claude Code the SDK runtime drives (its cli_path). auto       the installed claude when it is at least as new as the copy the SDK ships (or it ships none); else the shipped one -- versions unknown, the SDK keeps its own installed  the installed claude whenever there is one bundled    the SDK's own copy, always (the old behaviour) claude-agent-sdk 0.2.152 ships Claude Code 2.1.259, which answered "does not support this model" while the installed 2.1.309 -- the one phase 2 logs in and the CLI runtime runs -- served it: every SDK attempt failed first. |
| `stderr_lines` | `200` |  |
| `max_turns` | `24` | Fallback turn budget, used only by an agent whose definition sets none. Every agent below sets one, so raising *this* number changes nothing today -- it is here for an agent added later, and the honest word for it is "fallback" rather than "default".  To change the budget for all of them, use max_turns_override / --agent-max-turns. |
| `max_turns_override` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_MAX_TURNS:-0}"` | One turn budget for every agent, beating each definition's own (0 = off, the default, so the per-agent values stand: endpoint 10, package 10, bridge 12, strategy 10).  Written by --agent-max-turns. It has to beat the definitions rather than feed into them, because a value that merely fed in would lose to them and do nothing -- which is exactly what max_turns above does, and why a flag pointed at it would have been inert. Turns are the unit of agent thinking, and phase 4 is ~98% agent thinking, so this is the one lever that makes a long run genuinely *cheaper* rather than more overlapped -- --concurrency reduces waiting, this reduces work.  Lowering it is also the remedy the program itself prints when a stage runs out of wall clock ("lower mcp.agent.max_turns so the agent commits to an answer sooner"), advice that was unfollowable until this existed. Raising it usually wants more wall clock too: turns and timeout_seconds are independent budgets and the agent stops at whichever runs out first, so --agent-max-turns 30 on its own is often cut off around turn 6 -- and then timeout_turn_scale halves the budget for the next attempt. |
| `max_budget_usd` | `0.0` |  |
| `timeout_seconds` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-900}"` | Wall-clock ceiling for one agent stage, enforced by both runtimes.  A turn cap is not a time cap: a single turn can spend ten minutes in a web search, so without this a stage has no upper bound at all.  0 disables the ceiling. |
| `help_timeout_seconds` | `45` | How long `claude --help` may take when the CLI runtime reads which flags this claude supports. |
| `permission_mode` | `"acceptEdits"` |  |
| `allowed_tools` | `["Task", "Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep", "WebFetch", "WebS…` | Tools the discovery agents may use. Nothing here restricts Bash; each brief's hard rules keep it read-only towards the target. Each agent definition's own `tools` narrows this list, so Task reaches only a stage whose definition names no tools of its own -- the brief offers delegation only "if the Task tool is available". |
| `disallowed_tools` | `[]` |  |
| `workspace` | `"${cfg:paths.work_dir}/agent-workspace"` | Workspace where skills, agent definitions and generated artefacts live. Recreated on each run so the agents always see current instructions. |
| `skills_dir` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_SKILLS_DIR:-}"` | Where the SKILL.md files are copied from; empty means the ones packaged with initialize-claude-ai. Point this at your own directory to override the instructions. |
| `setting_sources` | `["project"]` | Which settings files the agent may load. 'project' makes the workspace's .claude/skills and .claude/agents visible. |
| `max_attempts` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS:-3}"` | How many times the agent may work the same stage before anything else is tried. An agent that abandons a stage on its first disappointing answer is not autonomous: most first answers fail for a correctable reason, and every retry is handed exactly what went wrong with the last one. Set to 1 for one shot. Written by --agent-max-attempts N for one run. |
| `credential_wall_settles_stage` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_CREDENTIAL_WALL_SETTLES:-true}"` | An endpoint that answered 401 or 403 settles its stage, so none of those attempts is spent re-finding it. The handshake did not complete and nothing pretends it did -- but the server was reached, it speaks for the target, and it is registered with its credential slot left empty; another attempt can only be refused by the same URL again, at five to eight minutes a time. false spends the remaining attempts looking for an endpoint that needs no credential at all. |
| `transient_free_retries` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_TRANSIENT_RETRIES:-3}"` | How many times a failure that was about *this moment* -- a service unavailable, a rate limit -- may be retried without spending one of the attempts above. A transient failure said nothing about the stage, so charging an attempt for it spends the agent's budget on bad luck; under --concurrency the bad luck is partly self-inflicted, and without this the flag could buy a fallback the agent never earned. 0 restores the older behaviour. |
| `prompt_register` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_PROMPT_REGISTER:-full}"` | How much brief the first attempt is given: full \| plain \| minimal. full    -- the whole brief, with what earlier stages found pasted inline. plain   -- shorter; the earlier findings stay on disk for the agent to read. minimal -- the target, what to establish, and the shape of the answer. A failure the model never got to read -- a request rejected before it was delivered, or one that ran out of clock -- moves the next attempt one step down this ladder, because appending an explanation to a brief that was never read cannot help and adding text to one that did not fit in the time cannot either. Start at "plain" on a deployment where the full brief keeps being rejected, and stop paying for the attempt that discovers it. |
| `max_list_items` | `8` | Longest list of anything -- probed paths, repositories, ports -- that is pasted into a brief verbatim. Past this, the agent is given the count, this many examples and the path to the file holding the rest. One endpoint stage records a hundred and sixty URLs; a brief repeating them spends the context window on data nobody acts on. |
| `max_prompt_findings_chars` | `4000` | Ceiling on the whole earlier-findings block in a brief, in characters. |
| `finding_value_chars` | `1500` | Ceiling on one value of an agent's `findings` as kept in the report, and on the findings of each earlier stage in the handoff to the next one, in characters of JSON. 0 keeps everything. |
| `previous_stage_findings_chars` | `6000` |  |
| `auth_claim_chars` | `300` | Ceiling on the reason an agent gives for proposing an endpoint with `requires_auth` (its `auth_evidence`), as carried on the candidate. |
| `timeout_turn_scale` | `0.5` | What the turn budget is multiplied by after a stage runs out of wall clock, so the next attempt aims at an answer it can finish rather than spending the same fifteen minutes again. Must be between 0 and 1. |
| `retry_models` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_RETRY_MODELS:-}"` | Models to try, in order, when a request is refused before the model reads it. Empty by default: whichever model the operator configured is the one to use, and naming another here would pin a model name into the program. Comma-separated, or a TOML list. The rotation is per address: a refusal moves *that* address to the next model it has not yet been on, never back to one that refused it, and never changes the model of another address in flight beside it under --concurrency.  The next address to start begins on the model the last rotation chose, which is what a one-at-a-time run has always done.  A retry model the deployment turns out not to serve is struck off for the run rather than taken as proof that the agent runtime is unusable. |
| `stop_when_nothing_changes` | `true` | A request refused again after the plain wording, with no shorter brief and no other model to send it to, is not sent a further time: it would be the same request, refused the same way.  The deterministic pipeline finishes the stage. |
| `retry_model_tiers` | `["sonnet", "haiku", "opus"]` | Where the rotation gets its models from when retry_models is empty: the tiers phase 3 already resolved, read back out of the variables it exported under each backend's [provision.*.env_names] model_tier pattern. Those ids came from the live backend, so they are real names for this deployment, which is the one thing a constant in the source could never be. Order is the order tried, and an empty list turns the derivation off, leaving the shorter brief as the only remedy for a refusal. |
| `fallback_to_traditional` | `true` | Let the deterministic pipeline finish a stage the agent could not settle, after every attempt above has been spent. This is a safety net, not a first resort; false makes an exhausted agent stage report its own verdict instead. |
| `progress_interval_seconds` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_PROGRESS_SECONDS:-30}"` | How often to print "still working" while an agent is thinking.  A stage can take many minutes and print nothing until it ends, which on screen is indistinguishable from a hung process.  0 turns the heartbeat off; so does console.progress = false, which turns off every progress line. |
| `verbose` | `"${INITIALIZE_CLAUDE_AI_AGENT_VERBOSE:-false}"` | Also name each tool call the agent makes, not just that it is still alive. Louder, and worth it when you are working out why a stage is slow. |
| `max_name_length` | `64` | Told to the agent of each stage when this machine already has registrations for the address at that tier; {registrations} lists each with how it answered when it was tried just before the agent started. An agent's word for a candidate's kind, mapped to the two the program takes ("stdio", "url") instead of refusing the candidate: two build.example.net candidates were discarded as "of unknown kind 'package'". A proposal's name longer than this (as a slug) is a description, not a name -- one proposal put its url, transport and how it was found there -- and the candidate is named from what it launches or reaches instead.  0: no limit. |
| `kind_from_shape` | `true` | A word in neither list ("bridge", "server") is decided by the candidate's shape: a command is stdio, a url is url -- when it carries exactly one. |
| `kind_aliases` | `{ package = "stdio", local = "stdio", process = "stdio", command =…` |  |
| `placeholder_patterns` | `[ …` | Text an agent copied from an example instead of filling in.  A candidate whose launch line, env, url or headers match one is refused, and the next attempt is told which placeholder it left -- one proposal for build.opensuse.org named /abs/path/osc-mcp, from the bridge-authoring skill's JSON example. Regular expressions, case-sensitive. |
| `existing_brief` | `"""` |  |
| `existing_brief_chars` | `200` | Characters of each registration's verdict kept in that brief. |
| `api_kind_brief` | `"""` | Told to the agent of tiers 2 and below when the target serves a kind of API (mcp.discovery.api_kinds): {kinds} names each with its URL, {search_terms} what to search by, {servers} the generic servers configured for it, each as the launch the run would trial.  Empty removes the paragraph. |
| `auth_wall_brief` | `"""` | Added to a tier-1 (endpoint) agent's brief: how to report an endpoint that refuses without a credential.  {variable} is the name the entry will read, {shape} what its value looks like and {obtain} where one comes from -- all three as the writer would choose them, auth profiles included.  Empty removes the paragraph. |
| `repair_brief` | `"""` | What the agent is told when an entry does not start (mcp.healing). The server name, the entry as written, the failure and what discovery knew about it are appended below this. |
